first.rationale: Currently favor shortening onboarding because it directly addresses the completion decline and has prior evidence of improving time-to-value and early adoption, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Verify that evidence against promotional pricing, which directly addresses competitive pressure but may carry margin, retention, or cohort-quality risks not resolved by the consolidated memory.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly matches the current onboarding decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, aligning with sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle: despite qualified-revenue lift, its verified cohort had 30-day retention down 12% and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Activation messaging remains plausible, but its evidence was not source-verified within this cycle's budget.

final2.rationale: Keep the shortened-onboarding experiment. The deeper competitive cut raises urgency but does not reverse the verified economics: the prior 40% SMB discount lifted qualified revenue 18% while reducing 30-day retention 12%, with the cohort failing before first renewal. Shortened onboarding instead improved completion 13%, time-to-value by 2.1 days, and retention 3%, directly addressing the current completion decline while supporting sustainable revenue. Price-related churn is a material unresolved risk, but launching a known-unsustainable discount without new evidence would optimize short-term acquisition at the expense of the primary objective.
